stances.claim: There is no common answer to the apparent contradiction of dismissals for the powerful and convictions for the rest; each case has unique facts and features, and the justices' philosophies of law differ -- to give one answer is to misunderstand judicial reality.

The dismissals of the three Marcos ill-gotten wealth cases trace to elementary procedural failures of the OSG and PCGG; while CJ won't repeat why, he affirms that a thorough investigation should identify which of the many solicitors-general, OSG prosecutors, PCGG chairs and commissioners over 30 years bears accountability.
stances.rhetorical_move: accountability-localization (cumulative failure must be disaggregated to individual officials)

stances.claim: The Africa decision (Dec 4, 2019) showed that the SBN does recover ill-gotten wealth from cronies when sufficient proof is presented; the simultaneous dismissal against Enrile, Imelda Marcos and Ferdinand Marcos Jr. shows that the procedural failure was selective, not universal.
stances.rhetorical_move: counter-example deployment (recovery is possible -- the failure was not categorical)

stances.claim: The Padaca MR's outcome depends on the SBN justices' legal philosophy -- strict-literal application would reiterate conviction; more liberal interpretation would create an acquittal possibility; CJ withholds his own view pending the MR.
stances.rhetorical_move: judicial-philosophy variable framing (outcome contingent on interpretive school)
stances.confidence: asserted with reservation ('I will just await her MR')

stances.claim: The GMA acquittal was based on failure to identify the 'main plunderer' and the JPE bail grant on advanced age + fragile health (not constitutional capital-offense bail test); both were strongly dissented from to no avail, but Bersamin's subsequent elevation to CJ functions as a partial defense of his ponencias -- though regardless, per Civil Code Art. 8, these verdicts 'form a part of (our) legal system.'
stances.rhetorical_move: controversial-ponencia legitimization (combining institutional-elevation argument and Civil Code finality)
stances.confidence: asserted with mixed neutrality and acceptance

stances.claim: The repetitive finger-pointing at prosecution failure across the dismissed/acquitted cases does NOT diminish Morales -- her reputation 'remains vibrant,' as evidenced by the AIM honorary doctorate of management being conferred on her this very morning.

notable_anecdotes: The timing precision -- 'at 9 o'clock this morning, Dec. 8' Morales receives the AIM honorary doctorate -- published in a column dated Dec 8, deployed as concurrent evidence that her reputation survives the downstream acquittals.

The 'why was Bersamin later named chief justice?' rhetorical defense of controversial ponencias -- a quietly devastating use of subsequent elevation as legitimation logic, presented as 'his supporters argue' (CJ does not personally adopt it).
Civil Code Art. 8 invoked to remind readers that controversial rulings -- once final -- 'form a part of (our) legal system' regardless of subsequent criticism.

The 30-year accountability problem -- many OSG/PCGG officials over 30 years bungled the Marcos cases, making single-actor accountability impossible without a 'thorough investigation' to disaggregate fault.
Republic v. Africa (Dec 4, 2019) -- the SBN simultaneously recovering from cronies AND dismissing against Enrile/Imelda/Marcos Jr. used as proof that the failure is selective, not categorical.
The 186-page Econg ponencia on Revilla -- the very length of the acquittal opinion implicitly raised as evidence of prosecutorial-failure cataloging.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban responds to the 'barrage of questions' from readers who could not reconcile why honest officials like Grace Padaca are convicted while alleged ill-gotten wealth cases against the Marcoses and their cronies are dismissed, why GMA and Bong Revilla were acquitted of humongous plunder, and why Juan Ponce Enrile -- facing a capital offense -- was granted bail. He frames the answers by rejecting the rhetorical-aggregate form of the question: 'No common answer can be given to these tough questions, some of which are really rhetorical. The cases have their own unique facts and features... and the justices... may have differing philosophies of law and may have viewed the cases from different perspectives.' First, the three ill-gotten wealth dismissals trace to OSG/PCGG procedural failures -- explained in his Nov 7 column -- and 30 years of cumulative bungling makes individual accountability hard to locate without a thorough investigation. Republic v. Africa (Dec 4, 2019) is offered as proof that recovery is possible against cronies even as it dismissed cases against Enrile, Imelda Marcos and Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for the same preponderance-of-evidence failure. Second, the Padaca MR's outcome will turn on whether the SBN justices apply law strictly and literally (reiteration of conviction) or liberally (acquittal possibility) -- CJ withholds his view pending the MR. Third, the GMA acquittal rested on failure to identify the 'main plunderer'; the JPE bail grant was grounded in advanced age and fragile health rather than the constitutional capital-offense bail test (evidence-of-guilt-strong) -- both Bersamin ponencias attracted strong dissent to no avail, but his subsequent elevation to CJ functions, per his supporters, as a partial vindication; regardless, Civil Code Art. 8 makes these verdicts 'form a part of (our) legal system.' Lastly, Justice Econg's 186-page Revilla acquittal repeated the prosecution's reasonable-doubt failure. CJ closes by defending Ombudsman Morales: despite the repetitive finger-pointing, her esteem 'remains vibrant,' as the Asian Institute of Management confers on her, at 9 a.m. this very morning of Dec 8, an Honorary Doctorate in Management.
